text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Syrian newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- U.N. General Assembly resolution strengthens Syria's, Palestinians' rights to land.
- Lebanese Prime Minister Hariri: Syria, Lebanon tracks on peace with Israel are inseparable.
- Israel shrugs off U.S. President Bill Clinton's criticism of Jewish settlements.
- Military siege imposed on Hebron university in the West Bank.
- U.S. disappointed at pace of Hebron talks between Israel and Palestinians.
- Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu sees accord with Palestinians soon.
- Clinton, Irish Prime Minister Bruton urge IRA to observe ceasefire.
- Cabinet reviews outcome of Syrian prime minister's visit to China and discusses latest Arab and international developments.
- U.N. General Assembly affirms Syria's right of sovereignty over the Golan and its resources.
- Cabinet discusses developments and praises the wise policy of president Assad in defence of the Arab causes. Syria committed to peace and return of occupied lands.
- Egyptian President Mubarak affirms importance of Arab solidarity.
- Cabinet discusses positive outcome of prime minister's visit to China.
- Lebanese Prime Minister Hariri praises the positive role of Syria's forces in keeping peace and stability in Lebanon.
